Maya — great to meet you yesterday. Quick response with an activation-first approach so procurement has what they need. High-level recommendation below, then I attached a one-page checklist and our private offer template.

Recommended term structure (pilot -> enterprise):
- Pilot: 3 months recommended (minimum work to de-risk integration). Usage-based billing at list rates, capped monthly spend (buyer-defined).
- Extended pilot: 6 months allowed if buyer needs longer time to measure ROI; include an early-conversion credit to push some pilot spend toward the annual commit if converted.
- Enterprise: 12 months (standard) with a stepped discount: 5% at $Xk, 10% at $Yk, 15% at $Zk committed ARR.

Approval mapping (typical buyer gates):
- Procurement: must approve PO terms and invoice flow (required).
- Legal: DPA + standard AWS addendum; legal review before signature on enterprise offer (often at pilot conversion).
- Finance / CFO: required for annual/committed discounts >10% or multi-year terms.

Seller checklist (what we will provide):
- SOC 2 Type II report (latest) + DPA draft
- Private Offer template (DocuSign-ready)
- Activation checklist: onboarding steps, SSO provisioning, technical POC milestones, billing contact + PO instructions

Attachments: PO_Activation_Checklist.pdf (pdf), Private_Offer_Template.docx (docx)

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share the attached checklist and template with you now.
2) If you want a 6-month pilot, flag that in your reply and I’ll request finance approval for the early-conversion credit (requires VP Revenue signoff).
3) If we need faster turnaround on approvals, we can do a two-signature flow where procurement signs the private offer and CFO signs the annual conversion amendment.

Looping in Aditya (finance) to call out discount thresholds and Hannah (legal) if we need special DPA terms.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call with procurement/legal if that speeds things up.

—
